blockingIssues.description: The new regression test hard-codes pre-reorg SHA-256 hashes for the six primers and asserts them forever. That overfits the one-time reorg and will fail later milestones that intentionally rewrite these same primers (for example f3-1 cert-manager, f4-1 traefik, f6-1/f6-2 istio, and f7-1 opa-gatekeeper).

codeReview.summary: The directory reorg itself is in place (category directories, no top-level primer files, updated path references, and a helper for subdir discovery), but the added test suite encodes the moved primer contents as immutable and therefore turns valid future primer work into false failures.

issues.description: Lines 70-101 freeze the six moved primer files to their pre-reorg SHA-256 values. The feature requirement only needs the move commit to be byte-identical; upcoming milestone features explicitly rewrite or refresh these primers, so this test will start failing as soon as those valid edits land.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The documented Python workflow and the recorded skill feedback do not match what actually happened. Mission docs say all Python commands should go through `uv run --directory engine/testgrid`, but this worker had to fall back to `uv pip install ... --python .venv/bin/python` plus `.venv/bin/python -m pytest/mypy/ruff`. The handoff still marks `followedProcedure: true` with no deviations.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: library/environment.md:21 says all Python invocations go through `uv run --directory engine/testgrid`. The F1.3 transcript shows `uv run --directory engine/testgrid pytest ...` failing, then `uv pip install pytest --python .venv/bin/python`, `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_integration_reorg.py -v`, and `uv pip install mypy ruff types-PyYAML --python .venv/bin/python`. The handoff file records `skillFeedback.followedProcedure: true` at lines 152-155.

sharedStateObservations.observation: There is no shared-state note warning future primer authors that F1.3's hash-based tests are only a reorg check and must be relaxed or removed before M3/M4/M6/M7 intentionally edit those primers.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: engine/testgrid/tests/test_integration_reorg.py:70-101 hard-codes hashes for cert-manager, traefik, istio-service-mesh, istio-ingress-gateway, gateway-api, and opa-gatekeeper. Upcoming features explicitly rewrite/refresh those same files in features.json:169-170 (f3-1 cert-manager), 288-289 (f4-1 traefik), 484-485 (f6-1 istio-service-mesh), 518-519 (f6-2 istio-ingress-gateway), and 584-585 (f7-1 opa-gatekeeper).

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission guidance does not make it explicit enough to stage only feature-owned paths when the repo starts with many untracked files. This feature commit bundled a wide set of unrelated additions, which obscures the intended reorg and makes later review harder.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `git show --stat --summary ec94adc` reports 28 files / 3942 insertions, including `engine/testgrid/dist/*`, `engine/testgrid/src/testgrid/render.py`, and other dashboard files outside the F1.3 description. `git ls-tree -r --name-only bc0074c -- engine/skills/chart-test-swarm/references/integrations` shows only `engine/skills/chart-test-swarm/references/integrations/gateway-api.md` was tracked before the commit; the worker transcript also notes the other primers were untracked before the move.

summary: Fail. The reorg itself looks correct, but the new `test_integration_reorg.py` suite turns a one-time byte-identical move into a permanent content freeze for primers that later milestones are supposed to rewrite, so this feature plants a future blocker.
